objective: Add a compact reusable BUKLOD Community Wall post presentation component by composing the existing canonical photo, video and engagement components without changing feed authorization, scope isolation, backend or runtime behavior.
productionBaselineEvidence: verified: this is DEV-only work and does not change or claim to deploy the production artifact. Repository production evidence records Android Production OTA workflow run #41291297116 completed 2026-11-01 from production source SHA 5d8214355a8a5ea12ecfd5c0c1e520fe4e263944. The PR base main SHA is the DEV integration baseline only; no new production fingerprint, RC, OTA or device adoption is asserted.
chosenApproach: Create a scope-agnostic presentation boundary used by Public and shared Organization/Sub-organization/Cluster renderers. Normalize the outer feed card shell while preserving feed-owned rich child renderers and all canonical media/engagement behavior.
selectionRationale: Compose established BUKLOD renderers instead of duplicating photo/video engines or reaction behavior. This minimizes media regressions and preserves the existing feed data and security boundaries.
preserveBehaviors: Existing dynamic one-to-four-photo collage geometry and source-aware single-photo framing
Existing private media URL resolution, cache and photo viewer behavior
Existing CommunityVideo poster, playback, network degradation and fullscreen behavior
Existing Buklod React reaction options, reaction counts and comment interactions
Exact Public, Organization, Sub-organization and Cluster feed authorization and isolation
Feed loading, pagination, realtime updates, inline ads and owner/moderation actions remain owned by existing containers
No Supabase, storage, RLS, native dependency, app config, runtime or OTA changes

Public Wall retains the existing author follow/menu controls, expandable caption and mention rendering, media URL hydration, video recovery, companion ads, comment previews, reaction details and internal sharing.
Organization, Sub-organization and Cluster Walls retain their scoped author metadata, owner actions, photo viewer, video recovery, report controls, comment/reaction behavior and internal sharing.
acceptanceChecks: Compact header renders author avatar/name, timestamp and audience/privacy indicator
Photo posts use the existing adaptive collage component
Video posts use the existing CommunityVideo renderer and poster path
Reaction, comment and share controls are exposed through explicit callbacks
No data fetching, Supabase mutation or authorization logic is added to the presentation component
Focused component contract tests and repository TypeScript/CI checks pass
Public Community Wall card root uses the shared theme-aware shell while retaining all existing author, caption, media, engagement and action behavior.
Shared wrapper does not fetch data, mutate posts, change media URL resolution, or alter feed authorization and scope isolation.
Public and all scoped walls use the same outer card surface, border, radius, inset and spacing tokens.
Legacy scoped postCard outer styling is not nested or applied a second time.
alternativeApproaches: Duplicate the photo grid and video player inside a new card (rejected: would fork rendering, caching, and recovery behavior).
Move feed loading and Supabase mutations into the card (rejected: would couple presentation to authorization and scope isolation).
Replace Public and Scoped feed renderers immediately (rejected: broad integration risk beyond the requested reusable component).
